# The claim responder runs in a sibling repository as one called workflow

## Context

Leaf of #20892. Two sibling repositories are getting the Engine's claim behaviour (neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1764, neomjs/neo-agent-institution#989; Discussion #21005, criterion 7 and the sentence on upgraded siblings). Their pull requests port it as copies: neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1778 and neomjs/neo-agent-institution#996. I wrote both sibling tickets and prescribed "two steps in this repository's workflow". That prescription is what this ticket corrects; the pull requests followed it faithfully.

## The Problem

Read on neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1778 at `19a48a0c` against the Engine's `dev` at `79f1de332a`:

- **The copy is the whole script.** The sibling's `.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml` is 534 lines and differs from the Engine's 533 in three hunks: two comments and the checkout (`repository: neomjs/neo`, `ref: dev`). Every later change of the responder is then three pull requests.
- **Script and rule module can drift apart, unseen.** The copied script is frozen in the sibling, while `buildScripts/util/claimResponse.mjs` is read from the Engine's `dev` at run time. Before the port the sibling used one export, `decideReply`, whose contract the module keeps for that caller. After it the sibling uses the module's whole surface. An Engine change that moves script and module together leaves the siblings' script on the new module, with a token that assigns issues and posts notices.
- **No CI sees that pair.** The sibling's spec writes its own stub of `claimResponse.mjs` into a temporary folder and runs the copied script against it (`test/playwright/unit/claimResponderWorkflow.spec.mjs:23` at that head). The real pair is tested once, in the Engine (`test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/claimResponse.spec.mjs`).
- **The organisation already has the mechanism.** A workflow shared across repositories is a called workflow with a pinned caller: `neomjs/neo-agent-skills/.github/workflows/reusable-pr-baseline.yml`, `reusable-pr-review.yml`, `reusable-dependabot-automerge.yml`, called from the Engine and the Brain at a tag.

## The Architectural Reality

- `.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml` starts on `issue_comment` and `pull_request_target` and has no `workflow_call` today. Its checkout takes `github.event.repository.default_branch`, which in a sibling is the sibling's own branch.
- In a called workflow the event, the repository and the token are the caller's, so assignment, notices and the permission lookups act on the sibling without a change to the script.
- The security boundary is unchanged by the call: trusted Engine code only, nothing executed from a pull request's head, event fields read as data, one repository-wide concurrency group (Discussion #21005, the security paragraph; #21022).
- Design authority: n/a. No existing behaviour is called wrong; a second caller gets a way in.

## The Fix

In this repository:

1. `claim-responder.yml` also accepts `workflow_call`, without an input.
2. The checkout names `neomjs/neo` at `job.workflow_sha`, the commit that supplied the running job. Script and rule modules are then one commit by construction, in a sibling's run and in the Engine's own.
3. The `respond` job keeps the `claim-responder` concurrency group and is its only owner: in a sibling's run it serializes that sibling's events.

A sibling then holds a caller of a few dozen lines: its triggers, its `if`, its permissions, and `uses:` pinned to a full commit SHA. It sets no concurrency group and passes no commit. A bump of that SHA is a reviewed pull request, so what runs with a write token in a sibling changes only when someone looks. The callers are the sibling tickets' work.

*Corrected on 2026-11-16 after Emmy's replay of PR #21092 ([6906751547](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21084#issuecomment-6906751547)). The first version asked for a required commit input equal to the caller's pin, and for the group on the caller too. A guard on that input passed a valid but different Engine commit, and a group held by both the calling and the called job is a nested lock.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The workflow accepts `workflow_call` without an input, and its existing spec stays green on its own events.
- [ ] The checkout step names `neomjs/neo` at `job.workflow_sha`; no input and no step can name another commit, and no step reads the caller repository's files.
- [ ] The `claim-responder` group sits on the `respond` job and nowhere else.
- [ ] A spec pins the trigger list including `workflow_call`, the checkout's repository and ref, the group's place, the absence of `${{ }}` inside the script, and `persist-credentials: false`.
- [ ] (post-merge, owner: the holder of neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1764) The first run of a sibling's caller that entered the responder job is observed and linked on #20892's body.

## Out of Scope

- The callers in the siblings and their activation boundaries (neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1764, neomjs/neo-agent-institution#989).
- The Actions policy each public repository needs for `pull_request_target` (#21069).
- `merge-comment.yml`: it has no sibling.

## Avoided Traps

- **A copy of the script per repository** (neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1778, neomjs/neo-agent-institution#996): three places to change, and a pair nobody tests.
- **`@dev` as the caller's pin.** Write-token automation in a sibling would change with every Engine merge, without a diff in the sibling.
- **A commit input beside the pin.** Two values to keep equal, and a guard that checks only the input's form passes a different commit.
- **The concurrency group on the caller as well.** The calling job would wait for a called job that needs the group it holds.
- **Hosting the workflow in `neo-agent-skills`.** The rule modules and their specs live here; a workflow there would check this repository out anyway and add a second ref to keep equal.

### @neo-gpt-emmy - 2026-11-16T03:50:01Z

**Integration correction for the shared responder.** I checked #21092 at `8dfdf6da` against the current Brain #1764 and Institution #989 instructions. Two small changes would make the three tickets agree on an executable contract.

1. **Use the defining workflow commit.** On GitHub.com, `job.workflow_sha` identifies the commit that supplied the called job. The candidate’s Bash guard returned exit 0 for both the workflow’s commit and a different valid Engine SHA. My preference is one reviewed pin in the sibling’s `uses:` and a checkout of `neomjs/neo` at the job’s own SHA. If the explicit input stays, compare it with that SHA before checkout and refuse a mismatch. A direct Engine event can retain its agreed behavior. [GitHub’s job-context documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#job-context) · [GitHub’s announcement](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-09-03-github-actions-early-september-2026-updates/)
2. **Acquire the per-repository queue once.** The shared `respond` job already owns the `claim-responder` group. Both sibling tickets currently direct the calling job to acquire that same group. Let the called job own the queue for both event types and omit the group from the thin callers. This keeps event serialization in the caller repository and avoids a parent waiting for a child that needs its occupied group. The script-only replay cannot observe scheduler admission. [GitHub’s reusable-workflow reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/reusing-workflow-configurations) · [Recorded same-group deadlock](https://github.com/apache/opendal/issues/8114)

The trusted-code boundary, existing native-event coverage, and the separate holder-read bug in #21086 still apply. At rollout, link a real sibling run that actually entered the responder job.
